paras: Lygisaurus macfarlani, also known commonly as the translucent litter-skink, and MacFarlan's skink, is a species of lizard in the subfamily Eugongylinae of the family Scincidae. The species is native to northeastern Australia and Papua New Guinea.
The specific name, macfarlani, is in honor of English missionary Samuel Macfarlane (1837–1911).
Adults of Lygisaurus macfarlani have an average snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 3.7 cm (1.5 in). The lower eyelid has a small transparent disc. There are usually six upper labials.
In Australia, Lygisaurus macfarlani is found in Northern Territory and Queensland. In Papua New Guinea, it is found in the Trans-Fly region and around Port Moresby.
Lygisaurus macfarlani occurs in a variety of natural habitats, including forest, savanna, shrubland, and grassland.
Lygisaurus macfarlani is terrestrial and diurnal.
